articles.title: Harry Kane se rinde ante Luis Díaz: revela la gran virtud que lo hace imparable
articles.standfirst: Harry Kane se deshace en elogios hacia Luis Díaz
articles.summary: Harry Kane se deshace en elogios hacia Luis Díaz
articles.body: El delantero inglés del Bayern Múnich, Harry Kane, ha llenado de elogios al extremo colombiano Luis Díaz, destacando no solo su desequilibrio individual, sino una faceta clave que muchas veces pasa desapercibida para los extremos tradicionales: su capacidad de ocupación de espacios y lectura de jugadas en el área rival. A pesar de que el conjunto bávaro tuvo un arranque de Bundesliga atípico —donde empataron ante el Schalke y el propio Díaz fue blanco de críticas tras errar algunas opciones de gol—, Kane respaldó firmemente al colombiano y a su compañero Michael Olise, restándole dramatismo al momento y destacando que la sociedad ofensiva que conforman es sumamente divertida y fructífera. En una entrevista concedida a TNT Sports, el atacante inglés explicó qué es lo que más valora de tener a 'Lucho' como socio en el frente de ataque, alejándose de los elogios habituales que solo se fijan en los regates vistosos. "Lo que más aprecio de Lucho es su habilidad para entrar en el área. Esos goles poco espectaculares, como me gusta llamarlos. A los extremos se les suele elogiar por su regate y sus jugadas espectaculares. Pero también hay que estar bien posicionado en el segundo palo y aprovechar los rebotes. Eso es precisamente lo que Lucho hace excepcionalmente bien", señaló Kane. Desde la llegada del guajiro al club alemán, ambos jugadores han compartido terreno de juego en 51 partidos, combinándose de manera directa en 13 anotaciones (11 tantos del inglés y 2 del colombiano), una cifra que esperan seguir aumentando a lo largo de esta temporada. Dejando atrás los tropiezos locales, el Bayern Múnich ya enfoca sus cañones en el debut de la fase de liga de la UEFA Champions League, donde se medirán este jueves en el Allianz Arena ante el Bodo Glimt de Noruega. Para Kane, el objetivo principal de este año es levantar la "orejona". "La temporada pasada, los pequeños detalles marcaron la diferencia. Esta temporada afrontamos el partido con la firme intención de que este sea nuestro año", expresó el delantero de 33 años, quien además descartó pensar en el retiro y aseguró sentirse en un gran momento físico para seguir cosechando títulos tanto a nivel de clubes como con su selección.

articles.title: Three LSU Tigers named SEC football players of the week
articles.summary: Multiple honors after dominant victory
articles.body:
The Southeastern Conference has announced the league's football players of the week following the SEC's openers to the 2026 season. Following LSU's lopsided victory, three Tigers were named in the honors including QB Sam Leavitt as Co-Offensive Player of the Week as well as OT Jordan Seaton and DE Jordan Ross as Offensive and Defensive Lineman of the Week, respectively.

Sharing the honor with Ole Miss WR Deuce Alexander, Leavitt finished last Saturday with three total touchdowns, two on the ground and one through the air. The QB not only finished as the game's top passer with 230 yards but also tied as the Tigers' leading rusher with another 113 yards. A school record 38 first downs were picked up against Clemson in Leavitt's debut, and the blockers up front were a big reason why, especially Seaton.

Jordan Seaton was a big factor in LSU's offensive success which led to 51 points being scored in the first game of the season. The transfer lineman from Colorado finished with no penalties committed or sacks allowed in his debut in Baton Rouge.

On the other side of the football, junior DE Jordan Ross was flying around the field in what was a truly impressive performance from Blake Baker's defense. Ross was at the center of perhaps the biggest play of the game on Saturday when he intercepted a pass in the first quarter and returned it back for a 30-yard pick-six, sending Death Valley into a frenzy. Ross was also credited with four tackles total, including a sack, and had a QB hurry in the game.

The Tigers were truly winning in every phase of the game in week one and LSU fans are hopeful this can just be a sign of things to come. Congratulations to all of these players.

articles.title: Inside the GB&I's stunning Walker Cup comeback: 'We were all pumped'
articles.summary: GB&I staged a remarkable comeback to defeat the USA at Lahinch, winning their first Walker Cup since 2015. How did they pull it off?
articles.body:
In a thrilling finale to the 51st Walker Cup , GB&I's golfers completed a remarkable recovery to beat the USA by a single point and lift this mighty clump of silverware for the first time since 2015.

On the final green of the final match on the course, Englishman Josh Hill held his nerve over a knee-knocker of a must-make birdie putt and made it to pip the world No 2, Tyler Watts, by one hole and secure the point that gave the hosts a 13 ½ - 12 ½ win.

This engrossing Sunday became so unbearably tense, it was akin to watching somebody trying to defuse a bomb and sweating over which wire to cut as the clock ticked down to zero.

Talk about amateur dramatics. Dean Robertson's men will be getting a lifetime achievement award from NODA.

Check out the best photos from the 2026 Walker Cup at Lahinch

NODA, by the way, is an association for, well, amateur dramatics. Anyway, this was one heck of a triumph at boisterous Lahinch on Ireland's west coast. The Guinness would be flowing in giddy abandon.

Leading by a point heading into the final day, GB&I found themselves on the back foot when the USA, aiming for a sixth win in a row in this grand transatlantic tussle, swept the Sunday foursomes 4-0 to assume command.

It looked like GB&I's hopes had crumbled like the ruins of the nearby Dough Castle. Out of the ashes of that session, however, came a tremendous resurgence as GB&I completed something of an historic fightback.

The US required just three-and-a-half points from the 10 singles to cart the cup back over the Atlantic.

Given that America's formidable strength in depth tends to come to the fore in the head-to-head jousts – they won the final day singles 8 ½ - 1 ½ the last time the sides met – it looked like mission impossible for GB&I.

The hosts were having none of that defeatist talk, though. "We were all pumped," said Luke Poulter, who channelled the spirit of his Ryder Cup hero dad, Ian, and pitched in with a singles success that helped turn the whole encounter on its head.

In the end, GB&I won the singles 7-3. That kind of scoreline in the session is such a rarity; it'll be getting valued at Sotheby's.

Back in 2001, when Peter McEvoy's dream team romped to victory at Sea Island in Georgia, GB&I won the closing singles 6 ½ - 1 ½. There were only eight matches in those days.

Lahinch in 2026 will be remembered for a truly wonderful turnaround. For the well-known Scot, Robertson, who suffered a hefty defeat in his first stint as GB&I skipper on US soil last year, this was a triumphant and highly emotional moment.

"I was thinking about my dad," said Robertson, who lost his father earlier this year.

"The US team were great this morning. But it can be such fine margins. We were playing great. I told the team that. We had to bring some energy and we did.

"I believed in the team the whole time."

That belief was underlined early on as GB&I burst out of the singles traps like whippets and won the top four encounters.

Stuart Grehan, the Amateur champion and the sole Irishman on the team, led from the front and downed the world No 1, Preston Stout, by 2&1, while Jack Whaley , the Yorkshireman who won the U.S. Amateur , was six-under for the 11 holes it took him to thump William Jennings 8&7.

Wins for Poulter and Tyler Weaver kept the hopes alive while Scotsman Niall Sheils Donegan added a half-point to the cause.

It looked like things would swing in the U.S.'s favor at the bottom of the order, though, but GB&I kept fighting.

Blairgowrie teenager Connor Graham, making his third Walker Cup appearance at just 19, illustrated this never-say-die spirit as he birdied both the 17th and 18th to come from two holes down against Miles Russell to pinch another half-point.

"I looked at the score, I knew I needed a half to keep it going," said Graham.

The U.S. was still within touching distance of at least retaining the cup, but Eliot Baker birdied the last to beat Walker Cup veteran Stewart Hagestad in another hugely important moment.

The stage was set for Hill to be the hero. And he was. A brilliant up-and-down from the greenside bunker on 18 gave him a last-gasp win over Watts.

"I asked Dean before my bunker shot, 'do I need a win or a half'," said Hill. "He said, 'A win.' I said, 'All right, let's do it.'"

articles.title: Dayton Dragons: New cast trying to make good on first-half success Midwest League playoffs start Tuesday
articles.summary: The Dayton Dragons are a perfect example of why the minor leagues split the 132-game season into halves. The players trying to win the first Midwest League c...
articles.body:
The Dayton Dragons are a perfect example of why the minor leagues split the 132-game season into halves.

The players trying to win the first Midwest League championship in club history are largely different from the players who won the East Division first-half championship to secure a berth into the semifinal round of the playoffs.

The first-half Dragons were led by players like Alfredo Duno, Carter Graham, Carlos Sanchez, Kien Vu, Yerlin Confidan, Ryan McCrystal and Peyton Stovall. They led a surge of eight wins in the final nine games of the first half.

Then they all went to AA Chattanooga. That team didn't make the playoffs.

But the holdovers and a slew of new young players get to play more baseball this week for Dayton. And Vu, infielder Johnny Ascanio and pitchers Victor Diaz and Jose Montero came back to Dayton last week to bolster the lineup and the staff. McCrystal, a catcher, came back early in the second half so he could play regularly instead of sit behind top prospect Duno in AA.

"It's a really cool thing to be able to play baseball that matters," McCrystal said. "We're always trying to develop and win every single game because I believe that's how you develop the best is to win together. But it's a really cool thing when it's win or go home."

Game 1 of the best-of-three series is Tuesday, Sept. 8 at second-half champion Great Lakes in Midland, Michigan. Game 2 is in Dayton on Thursday followed by Game 3 on Friday, if necessary.

The Loons led most of the first half before the Dragons clawed past them. The Loons won the second half with a 39-26 record and own the best overall record in the division at 75-54. The Dragons were 28-36 in the second half and 67-63 overall.

This team is led by 2026 draft picks Justin Lebron and Eric Becker, 2025 picks Vu and Ty Doucette and 2024 high-school pick Tyson Lewis and second-year Dragon John Michael Faile. The starting pitchers planned for the three-game series are Edgar Colon, Kyle McCoy and Mason Morris.

"It's been fun," said Lebron who bats leadoff, hits for power and gets on base. "Coming out here each and every day, playing for each other and getting ready for the playoffs."

One constant is Faile, whose powerful bat has helped the Dragons finish the final two weeks at 7-5 and gain a little momentum.

"We had a great team the first half, a team that really came together from the first game from opening night, and now a lot of those guys are moved on, which is awesome for them," he said. "This team's different. We have a lot of younger guys, a whole different team, and so this group's coming together. Hopefully, coming together at the right time, and I think we can make a special run and see what happens."

The experienced Dayton players — McCrystal, Faile, McCoy, reliever Jimmy Romano — are the clubhouse leaders that a team full of new players needs.

"Those guys have kept the team pretty even keeled," Becker said.

McCrystal is in a unique position to lead the entire team through his attitude because of his experience and because he is a catcher working with young pitchers. He got a taste of AA, then came back, not because he couldn't play at AA, but because the Reds wanted him to play.

He's relied on his faith and the counsel of his fiancé to work through the difficulties of the grind, learning not to take bad games home and accepting that Dayton is where he belongs for now.

"Understanding that you're back here for a reason and learning how to be a leader, learning how to lead," McCrysytal said. "It's a tough thing because coming back here, it's not like I played bad there."

Hitting coach Troy Gingrich has helped McCrystal see what he should focus on through the ups and downs of a long season.

"Troy said to me one time, and it's kind of stuck with me, you're trying to look at the whole dartboard when I'm just looking at the bull's-eye," McCrystal said. "You can't look at all the negatives when there's a ton of positives as well. But you need to try and keep your eyes focused on the bull's-eye, which is the positive things, the things that God's blessed. And then you'll be able to ignore the negatives, and the more you do that, the better that you're going to be."

That's the Dragons' chore this week. Ignore the negatives of a second-half losing record, and focus on the playoff opportunity.

"That's all you can really do," Lebron said. "Just got to keep playing baseball."

articles.title: Zheng wins set from 5-0 down again to stun Swiatek
articles.summary: Zheng Qinwen wins a set from 5-0 down for the second successive match as she shocks Iga Swiatek to reach the US Open quarter-finals.
articles.body:
Zheng Qinwen won a set from 5-0 down for the second match in succession as she extended her fantastic US Open run by beating former champion Iga Swiatek to reach the quarter-finals.

Zheng, the reigning Olympic champion and former world number four, dropped outside the world's top 100 earlier this year while struggling to regain her best form following elbow surgery in July 2025.

The 23-year-old from China had trailed Madison Keys 5-0 in the deciding set of their third-round match on Saturday before winning seven successive games to secure her spot in round four.

And Zheng was 5-0 down in the opening set against Poland's eighth seed Swiatek, but won 13 of the next 16 games on Arthur Ashe Stadium to set up a quarter-final against either Naomi Osaka or Elena Rybakina.

The second set was on serve until the seventh game, when Zheng crushed a powerful backhand return winner to secure a crucial break, and she broke again two games later to complete a 7-5 6-3 victory.

This latest win - her seventh in a row in New York having come through three rounds of qualifying - will put her back to the brink of the top 50.

"The more matches I play, the more rhythm I have on court," said Zheng.

"People have asked me if I'm tired and when I arrived I was not tired at all. I felt really pumped for my match, trying to reach better levels here and enjoy this fantastic stadium."

Elsewhere, French Open winner Mirra Andreeva recovered from losing the first set to Anastasia Potapova to reach the last eight in New York for the first time in her career.

Zheng's only win in eight previous meetings against Swiatek was in the semi-finals of the 2024 Olympics on her way to singles gold in Paris.

She will discover her quarter-final opponent later on Monday, when former US Open champion Osaka plays second seed Rybakina.

The most recent qualifier to reach this stage of the women's draw at the US Open was Great Britain's Emma Raducanu, who went on to win the title in 2021.

And Zheng is not the first female qualifier to perform well at a Grand Slam in 2026 - Poland's Maja Chwalinska, who began the French Open at 114th in the world, lost to Russian teenager Andreeva in the final at Roland Garros.

For Swiatek, 25, a fourth-round exit is a disappointing end to her Grand Slam season, with a quarter-final appearance at the Australian Open her best result.

She was beaten in round four of the French Open, while the defence of her Wimbledon title ended in the third round.

It means that, for the first time since 2021, Swiatek will end a year without winning one of the sport's four majors.

Swiatek, who received treatment to her left thigh when leading 2-1 in the second set, had entered the US Open in excellent form by winning the WTA 1000 event in Toronto and getting to the semi-finals in Cincinnati, while she had progressed through to round four without dropping a set.

Andreeva through against 'warrior' Potapova

Andreeva, 19, was severely tested by Potapova until the 24th seed injured her knee in what proved to be the final game of their match on Louis Armstrong Stadium.

Potapova seemed to twist or hyperextend her knee while attempting to hit a ball on the run from the baseline and Andreeva was across quickly to check on her grounded opponent.

Russia-born Potapova, who represents Austria, returned to the court after receiving treatment but lost the remaining points in her service game, confirming her exit from the tournament.

Fifth seed Andreeva, who won 5-7 6-4 6-3, said: "Anastasia is my good friend and seeing what a battle we had and seeing her fall like that in the last game, it's not easy.

"I told her that she's been playing amazing and having one of her best seasons. I'm sure she'll come back even stronger - she's a warrior and an even better fighter than me."

Andreeva will play either Coco Gauff or Iva Jovic, who play their all-American fourth-round match in Monday's night session, in the quarter-finals.

articles.title: Blue Jays predicted by ESPN to pull off incredible postseason comeback
articles.summary: This bold prediction does actually have a good chance of coming true.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays came into the 2026 MLB season looking like one of the top teams in all of baseball. But a rough first half had them as trade-deadline sellers. They shipped off Daulton Varsho and Kevin Gausman at the deadline.

But now, with under a month to go in the MLB regular season, they're actually in the fight for the third and final AL Wild Card spot. Sitting just 1.0 game back, they may make the postseason.

ESPN polled 15 MLB experts for their prediction of which AL team will make the third wild card spot. Of those 15 votes, 10 predicted that the Blue Jays would wind up making the playoffs as that third wild card team.

Blue Jays predicted to make MLB postseason by 10-out-of-15 ESPN analysts

The results of this ESPN poll had the Blue Jays receiving 10 votes, the Cleveland Guardians receiving four votes, and the Texas Rangers the last remaining vote.

While the Guardians might have a 1.0 game lead over the Blue Jays entering play on Labor Day, Toronto is predicted by two-thirds of ESPN's MLB analysts, experts, and insiders to make up the difference in the final weeks of the year.

It would not be a surprise at all if the Blue Jays wound up securing this spot, as they're playing well lately and were just in the postseason one year ago.

Sure, the 2026 season hasn't gone well for the most part, but this current Blue Jays squad has what it takes to sneak into the postseason.

The Blue Jays have a .748 OPS in the last few weeks, which is 12th-best in MLB in that span, and is much better than the Guardians at 22nd place with a .685 OPS.

While their pitching might be similar, with Dylan Cease and Parker Messick being among the best pitchers in MLB this season, the offense is the big difference.

So long as the Blue Jays can hang around in the AL wild card, with a relatively easy schedule against the Athletics , Baltimore Orioles , Detroit Tigers , Rangers, Orioles again, and Cincinnati Reds , securing that third Wild Card spot is very possible.

This 10-out-of-15 prediction from ESPN is not a huge surprise, as the Blue Jays are well set up to sneak into October after a rough start to their 2026 MLB season.

articles.title: David Sánchez ya ve en septiembre campeón al Barça: "Veremos si le da para Europa..."
articles.standfirst: El periodista catalán estará los lunes en Otra Ronda, el nuevo programa de Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El periodista catalán estará los lunes en Otra Ronda, el nuevo programa de Radio MARCA
articles.body: David Sánchez volvió a casa. El periodista regresó a los micrófonos de Radio MARCA y lo hizo en Otra Ronda, el nuevo programa nocturno de la radio del deporte presentado por Carlos Vicente 'Chitu'. Una charla distendida que dejó también varias reflexiones sobre la actualidad del fútbol, con el Barcelona, el Real Madrid, Mourinho y Mbappé como protagonistas. Uno de los grandes titulares de la conversación llegó cuando Sánchez se mojó sobre la pelea por LaLiga. Su apuesta es clara: el Barcelona será campeón. "Yo creo que la Liga la va a ganar el Barça bastante bien", aseguró. El periodista considera que el conjunto azulgrana está jugando mejor que el Real Madrid y que esa superioridad futbolística puede marcar la diferencia durante el campeonato. Sánchez, eso sí, no descarta que el equipo blanco pueda imponerse en los dos Clásicos. El problema, según su análisis, estaría en los partidos ante rivales que se repliegan y dificultan el juego del conjunto madridista: "No descarto que el Madrid le gane los dos Clásicos al Barça, pero van a perder la Liga porque se van a dejar puntos cuando se encuentre equipos de estos que se le encierran". La conversación también puso el foco en el Real Madrid y en la figura de José Mourinho. Sánchez reconoció que el técnico portugués le parece "un fenómeno" y un personaje "espectacular" para el fútbol, aunque tiene dudas sobre su capacidad para volver a dirigir a un equipo de la máxima exigencia. "Puede ser el entrenador que ponga orden en el vestuario, pero el orden táctico yo creo que ya se le pasa a Mourinho", explicó. En su opinión, el conjunto blanco atraviesa actualmente "un problema futbolístico de verdad". Y señaló un nombre que, a su juicio, habría cambiado el escenario: Rodri. "Yo sigo pensando, no es por tocarle el amor a los madridistas, yo creo que el no fichar a Rodri es un error tremendo. Yo creo que con Rodri el Madrid jugaría otra cosa", afirmó. Otro de los asuntos de actualidad fue Kylian Mbappé y sus declaraciones en rueda de prensa sobre su candidatura al Balón de Oro. Sánchez fue contundente con el delantero francés y considera que sus palabras suponen el inicio oficial de una campaña por el premio. "Me parece bastante cutre", señaló sobre el hecho de que el futbolista se señale públicamente como candidato. Para Sánchez, la temporada de Mbappé debe analizarse también desde el rendimiento colectivo. El periodista también interpretó las declaraciones del delantero como un mensaje relacionado con su papel dentro del equipo y su escasa implicación defensiva: "A mí me pagan para marcar goles y para que mis cifras sean superiores a las de Raphinha, Dembélé y el otro, el de la moto. Si quieren defender, que fichen a más defensas". Durante la charla, Chitu y David Sánchez repasaron también algunos de los protagonistas que ya han pasado por Otra Ronda. Luis de la Fuente, Robert Lewandowski, Carlos Vicente y Maluma han sido algunos de los primeros padrinos del nuevo espacio de Radio MARCA. Sánchez destacó especialmente su encuentro con Lewandowski, al que definió como "un delantero de leyenda" y elogió por el rendimiento que ha ofrecido durante su etapa en el Barcelona. "Yo lo hubiese renovado una temporada más", reconoció sobre el delantero polaco. La conversación sirvió así para abrir la semana en Otra Ronda, con Chitu al frente y David Sánchez como uno de los invitados habituales de los lunes en el nuevo programa nocturno de Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Who is Carly Korwin? Spencer Korwin’s widow reveals ‘worst day’ after former Team USA triathlete’s tragic drowning
articles.summary: International Sports News: Former Team USA triathlete Spencer Korwin’s widow Carly Korwin broke down in tears while remembering her husband at his funeral in New York on Sunday..
articles.body: Former Team USA triathlete Spencer Korwin’s widow Carly Korwin broke down in tears while remembering her husband at his funeral in New York on Sunday. Spencer, 38, died after drowning during a family vacation on Shelter Island on September 2. His body was found beneath the dock at The Pridwin Hotel several hours after he went missing during a morning swim. Carly spoke about their marriage, their two young daughters and the life they had built together. She called Spencer the love of her life and said she still could not accept that he was gone. The funeral was held at Temple Israel.Who is Carly Korwin, Spencer Korwin’s widow?Carly Korwin, née Shapiro, is Spencer Korwin’s widow. She is a Syracuse University graduate and works in advertising and marketing in New York City. Carly and Spencer reconnected and began dating years after college before getting married. They lived in Manhattan and had two daughters, Sadie, 4, and Colette, 1.Carly became the focus of attention after giving an emotional eulogy for Spencer. Speaking through tears, she said, “This is a nightmare. This is the worst day of my life. I can’t accept that this is real and that Spencer is not going to come home.”She then spoke about the man he was to her and their children.“Spencer was more than I could ever have dreamed of when it came to a husband, a father, and a friend. He was the best human I have ever met, and he was the love of my life.“We had the most beautiful and special once-in-a-lifetime type of love, and we knew it.“We always said forever isn’t long enough. And I will never be able to make sense as to why this incredible life we built together, filled with happiness and so much love, was ripped away from us in an instant.”Carly also remembered the small things Spencer did for his family. “He wrote me and the girls notes all the time and hung them around the apartment,” she said.“He was filled with surprises and hugs just because… he had automated texts set up twice a day just to remind me that he loves me, I’m a wonderful mom and wife.“I know the girls will never stop missing him, and he will forever be their hero.”What happened to Spencer Korwin on Shelter Island?Spencer was on vacation with Carly and their daughters when he went into the water near the hotel dock at about 8 a.m. on September 2. When he did not return, Carly alerted hotel staff, who contacted emergency services. A search involving marine and air units followed, and divers found his body underwater near the dock around 3 p.m.The Shelter Island Police Department said the death is believed to be accidental, while the official cause remains pending the medical examiner’s report. Police also said the waters can have strong currents because of the narrow passage and that tides and boat traffic are always factors.Spencer was a Syracuse University graduate and represented Team USA at the 2012 Triathlon World Championship in Auckland, New Zealand. He later moved into health and wellness, founding Korwin Health & Wellness in 2021 and previously working as a trainer for SportsLab NYC.The details of Carly’s tribute were reported by the Daily Mail, while local authorities and other reports have confirmed the circumstances surrounding Spencer’s death.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fans disagree with Portland Thorns over reason for ejection in XX-XY apparel dispute: 'They are lying'
articles.summary: Video shows Portland Thorns fans removed from Providence Park over women's sports apparel, with Amy Sousa denying claims of distributing materials.
articles.body: A Portland Thorns spokesperson said eight fans were removed from Providence Park during the NWSL club’s Sept. 6 match against the Washington Spirit for distributing "unapproved materials," a claim the group disputes. In a statement sent to OutKick, the Thorns spokesperson said, "During our September 6 match against the Washington Spirit, individuals were removed from Providence Park for distributing unapproved materials, a violation of the Fan Experience Guidelines at the stadium. Our priority remains fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment for every fan at Providence Park." The Thorns spokesperson added that the matter is still being investigated. Amy Sousa, who was part of the group, denied the allegation, saying the fans were targeted for political reasons and were expressing support for women’s sports. WNBA FACES GROWING SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM MOVEMENT AS NEW RALLIES ARE SET FOR FEVER GAMES IN OREGON, MINNESOTA "We did not distribute any materials. We came armed with copies of their own code of conduct and we followed it to the letter," Sousa said in a statement sent to OutKick. "They are lying about us. They have violated our rights. My group was targeted for political beliefs I speak about online." Sunday at Providence Park The group was wearing XX-XY Athletics apparel and shirts bearing messages including "Save Women’s Sports," "Girls just wanna have fundamental rights," "Woman" and "It’s common sense." Video showed Sousa questioning her removal after she had entered the stadium and taken her seat. Security handed the group of eight a Providence Park notice and escorted them out after a dispute over whether they were distributing materials, a claim Sousa denies. The notice cited a Code of Conduct violation and warned of additional penalties, including a possible ban. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS OPEN UP ON ENCOUNTER WITH SECURITY, PRO-TRANS FANS IN LATEST WNBA CULTURE CLASH Ahead of the match, Sousa said she brought five printed copies of the NWSL and Providence Park codes of conduct after receiving a message from local activist Hannah Perry. Sousa denies distributing materials Sousa said Perry had warned her that she was contacting officials about the group’s planned attendance, so she wanted to be prepared to reference the venue’s rules. Sousa also said the group only shared the printed copies among themselves while seated. WNBA ADMITS SECURITY IN ATLANTA WAS WRONG TO MAKE FANS COVER SHIRTS AT DREAM-FEVER GAME "We only shared them to our own group while seated facing each other. We only brought five," she said. "If we ‘distributed’ anything, they would have it on video." Sousa also said the group’s XX-XY clothing was covered when they initially entered the stadium. MOM AND DAUGHTER TOLD TO COVER UP XX-XY T-SHIRTS, SAY THEY WERE THREATENED WITH EJECTION AT FEVER-DREAM GAME "And our XX/XY Clothes were not visible when we arrived," Sousa said. Group asked to leave local bar The dispute continued after the group left Providence Park. After leaving, the group went to The Sports Bra, a Portland bar focused on women’s sports. Members were later asked to leave. Video from inside the bar showed a staff member ordering the group to leave after accusing them of wearing "transphobic" clothing. The Sports Bra later released a statement on social media defending its decision. "At The Sports Bra, our mission is simple: support, promote, and empower ALL girls and women in sports," the bar said. "To be clear: trans girls are girls, and trans women are women." The statement added that while it welcomes people of every identity and background, it does "not tolerate messages or conduct that demean or exclude the very community we exist to serve and celebrate." "On Sunday, Sept. 6, a group entered wearing apparel with messages advocating for the exclusion of trans women from sports," the statement continued. "When our team respectfully gave the group notice to cover the anti-trans messaging or leave, they chose to leave." articles.title: SEC teams went 16-0 in Week 1, is the conference back on top of college football world?
articles.summary: The SEC went 16-0 in week one, but after three straight Big Ten national championships, do the results really shift the college football hierarchy?
articles.body: After three straight national championship wins, few would argue that the Big Ten has become the top conference in college football. Three years, three different teams, including a 16-0 season from the Indiana Hoosiers that coaches like Texas' Steve Sarkisian believed were essentially impossible in the modern era. Entering the 2026 season, most believed that the Big Ten would once again be the cream of the college football crop, thanks to Ohio State and Oregon topping the country in most human, and computer, ranking systems. But fast forward through week one's results, and there's one, very familiar, conference tooting its own horn about where it ranks in the college football hierarchy: the SEC. HAS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP PICTURE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL ALREADY CHANGED AFTER A STUNNING FIRST WEEK? The SEC through week one went 16-0, an impressive feat for any conference, and an indication that their impressive depth will once again be relevant in 2026. Some fans have been quick to suggest that this means the SEC is back on top, that the Playoff and national championship will once again run through the previously dominant conference. But how much can we learn about where the SEC sits? Or at least, where these individual teams sit in the season-long picture? Well, a little, and also, not very much. Let's take a quick look at how the SEC got to 16-0 and what it all means. Missouri was the first win of the weekend, with a 56-14 drubbing of Arkansas Pine-Bluff. Nothing to glean from that. On Friday, Oklahoma shut out UTEP 51-0. The Miners were 127th out of 138 FBS teams in SP+ heading into the season, but still, the Sooners did what they needed to do against a bad team. Alabama handled East Carolina, South Carolina throttled Kent State, Kentucky beat up on Youngstown State, Georgia predictably beat down Tennessee State, Tennessee won 56-9 over Furman, Texas took care of Texas State, Texas A&M shut out Missouri State, and Mississippi State won 62-13 over UL Monroe. Despite giving up 14 first half points to Florida Atlantic, the Gators cruised 66-21. Arkansas was unimpressive in a 31-14 win over FCS North Alabama, and Vanderbilt stretched a 15-9 halftime lead over Austin Peay into a 28-9 win. LSU'S LANE KIFFIN ADMITS HE LET TIGER STADIUM WEATHER DELAY DRAG ON IN ORDER TO HURT CLEMSON All better than Rutgers' performance, without question. But these were all games that the SEC team should win easily, and they did. The three other games, LSU-Clemson, Ole Miss-Louisville, and Auburn-Baylor, said a bit more about where the conference sits. LSU, of course, dismantled and humiliated Clemson, and immediately made a strong case as a conference challenger alongside Texas, Georgia, and Alabama. Auburn was favored by 6.5 points, but the game turned out to be evenly matched. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM After a back-and-forth battle, Baylor went for the aggressive play to win in regulation instead of sending the game to overtime, only to come up inches short of a two-point conversion to take an 18-17 lead. An evenly matched game between two evenly matched teams that doesn't tell us much about which team is "better," necessarily, particularly given Auburn's unimpressive performance against the spread. Baylor after all, was No. 54 in preseason SP+, while Auburn was No. 26. They should have won, and they did, but without answering questions about their prognosis for the rest of the season. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Similarly, Ole Miss should have handled Louisville. They were favored by 6.5 points, came into the season 11 places ahead of Louisville in SP+, and won on a walk-off field goal. Louisville, if anything, slightly outplayed the Rebels, racking up 6.9 yards per play to 6.3 for Ole Miss. They were better at protecting the ball and had a higher average yards per carry, while adding 10.6 yards per attempt passing. GREG SANKEY INSISTS SEC IS 'STRONGEST LEAGUE' DESPITE BIG TEN WINNING THREE STRAIGHT NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIPS Ole Miss gets credit for the win, as they should, but again, they were favored, should have won, and were fortunate to do so. Which is where this all shakes out. In the three games against other Power 4 schools, the SEC team was favored by 6.5, 6.5, and 10 points. In two of those games, they failed to cover and won what amounts to a toss-up. In the other? Well, let's just say LSU set the Clemson program back years. articles.title: Titans LB Cedric Gray Injured in UTV Accident
articles.summary: The standout linebacker suffered a concussion and minor injuries during a weekend off-road mishap. Tennessee now faces roster uncertainty ahead of a pivotal...
articles.body:
It was a relatively normal day for the Tennessee Titans on Labor Day as players spoke to the media in the locker room.

We got to hear from the likes of J.C. Latham, Elic Ayomanor, Wan'Dale Robinson, Hendon Hooker and Austin Schlottmann .

Then, there was some breaking injury news for the Titans.

ESPN's Turron Davenport shared that Titans linebacker Cedric Gray had been in a UTV accident over the weekend and was going to be in concussion protocol. Davenport clarified that the accident had nothing to do with reckless driving and that there was no alcohol involved.

The Titans also released a statement on the accident.

"Over the weekend, Cedric Gray was involved in a UTV accident in Tennessee and sustained a concussion and minor injuries," the statement read. "We look forward to Cedric returning to the field soon and in full health when he clears the NFL's concussion protocol."

Hopefully, the concussion isn't very severe, because Gray was a major contributor to this team last year.

He was drafted out of North Carolina in 2024. He was used as a rotational player as a rookie, appearing in seven games and recording 22 total tackles.

Gray then had a massive breakout season, recording 164 total tackles, seven tackles for loss, one sack, and two fumble recoveries.

Gray finished with the fourth-most total tackles in the NFL last season. Only Devin White (174), Jack Campbell (176) and Jordyn Brooks (183) had more total tackles than Gray did in 2025.

He is expected to reprise his role as one of the Titans' starting linebackers this year, even with Robert Saleh moving the team to a 4-3 defense.

The injury news couldn't have come at a worse time for the Titans, as they prepare to take on the New York Jets on Sunday.

It will be the first time that Saleh has faced the Jets as head coach of another team since he was fired by them in 2024.

This could make things interesting for the linebacker room.

The Titans recently placed Mohamoud Diabate on the practice squad and may need to bring him back to the active roster depending on the severity of Gray's concussion.

We'll have to wait and see for more updates on Gray's status ahead of Sunday's game. The Titans may have a roster decision to make if Gray is out for a significant amount of time.

Either way, the Titans face the Jets on Sunday at noon CT on CBS.

articles.summary: Is Atlanta Hawks swingman Dyson Daniels injured?
articles.body:
Atlanta Hawks forward Dyson Daniels is not dealing with an injury, according to Brad Rowland .

Here is what the Hawks insider recently shared on X: "I know there is a social media video circulating with Dyson Daniels wearing something on his right arm that caused a bit of a stir. Was told by a source this morning that there is no injury."

Daniels was a participant in a minicamp with the Australia men's basketball national team in early August. He did not get injured while playing.

All signs point to Daniels being ready to go for Atlanta training camp, which begins soon.

For the Hawks last season, Daniels played in 76 games. He averaged 11.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 2.0 steals and 0.4 blocks per game while shooting 51.7% from the field, 18.8% from beyond the arc and 61.5% from the free-throw line.

The 23-year-old Daniels made the All-Defensive Second Team last season. He made the All-Defensive First Team and won the Most Improved Player of the Year award in his first season with the Hawks.

Atlanta lost to the New York Knicks in the first round of the 2026 playoffs, but remember, the Hawks were the only team to beat the Knicks twice in the 2026 postseason.

That shows how good the Hawks will be moving forward.

The Hawks had a busy offseason. They signed CJ McCollum to an extension, re-signed Jock Landale, acquired Devin Carter from the Sacramento Kings, Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder and Ryan Nembhard from the Dallas Mavericks and drafted Kingston Flemings, Zuby Ejiofor and Henri Veesaar in the 2026 draft.

Moving forward, Atlanta's core is Dort, Wiggins, McCollum, Jalen Johnson , Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Onyeka Okongwu .

Atlanta is expected to start McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Daniels, Johnson and Okongwu next season. The Hawks begin the 2026-27 regular season on the road against the Orlando Magic.

"I don't compare ourselves to others," McCollum told HoopsHype about the Hawks' future. "Right now, it's about focusing on getting better individually and collectively. We can't control how other teams look. You can control your approach to the game. Teams will get better and evolve.

"For us, it's about focusing on improving our intangibles, understanding our schemes, and what Quin wants from us. Then, building on the momentum and experience that we had playing in the playoffs in a big environment on the road and in our home games. We played against a team that won the NBA Finals. All those things help you as you go into a new season."

articles.title: Braves at Phillies series recap: Atlanta holds serve and keeps their nerve
articles.summary: The Braves went in with a four-game lead in the division. The Braves left town with a four-game lead in the division.
articles.body:
Four down, three to go. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies have now played four of the seven games they've got scheduled against each other here in September and so far, the Braves can at least rest easy knowing that they held serve in the division. Sure, it would've been great to see the Braves win the series or even sweep it but being realistic, a road split was a decent result and as we always say, "you always take a four-game split on the road."

So, how did Atlanta go about earning the split in order to make sure that their four-game lead in the division remained at four games once they left town? Let's not waste any more time and hop right into it, shall we?

Chris Sale just keeps on making it happen, doesn't he? While this wasn't on the same level as that epic complete game shutout that he pulled off against the Dodgers not too long ago, the fact that he was able to pitch six strong innings while holding Philadelphia to just two runs and leaving the game with a lead was absolutely huge. The only Phillies hitter who really had any sort of idea as to how to really get to Sale on the night was Alec Bohm, whose RBI double in the second and his dinger in the fourth served as the only blemishes on Sale's record for the night. Outside of that, Sale gave the Braves exactly what they needed on this particular night.

While this was going on, Atlanta's lineup essentially rode a three-run inning in the second nearly all the way to the house. Like manna from heaven, the Braves managed to get a real rally going off of Cristopher Sánchez and it peaked with a three-hitter run where Austin Riley bounced one into right field (where Bryce Harper continued to show why it's probably not a great idea to have him back in the outfield) for an RBI single, Ha-Seong Kim continued his return to relevancy with a productive out that plated Mauricio Dubón from third base and then Ronald Acuña Jr. fired off his first salvo of the weekend with an RBI single to make it 3-0 Braves.

Atlanta had a 3-2 lead heading into the eighth before a big fly gave Atlanta the breathing room they needed in order to make it a relatively comfortable finish. Mike Yastrzemki came through with a pinch-hit, one-out walk against Orion Kerkering and then Mauricio Dubón popped one into the seats in left field for a two-run shot that put the Braves out ahead by three. Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias held down the fort in their relief innings and Atlant was halfway towards the split they needed.

Unfortunately, it was Philadelphia's turn to go up 3-0 early on in the contest. The Braves wasted a bases-loaded opportunity against Zack Wheeler in the first inning and as it turns out, that was the golden opportunity for the Braves against Wheeler as he ended up cruising through six innings with only one run given up. Meanwhile, Martín Pérez got tagged for four runs in just 3.2 innings as he struggled to find the strike zone for most of his outing.

Four walks for Pérez in the first basically led to two runs being scored by the Phillies and then a productive out from Kyle Schwarber cashed in a leadoff triple in the second from Derek Hill. Schwarber then proceeded to add Philadelphia's fourth run in his usual way in the fourth inning — via dinger. That'd be the first of three dingers on the weekend for Schwarber, who currently has five homers against the Braves so far this season. Good grief. For what it's worth, he's also got six dingers agains the Mets so basically he's the ultimate crowd-pleaser up there in Philadelphia.

Anyways, Atlanta's offense couldn't hack it against José Alvarado and Jhoan Duran on this particular night, though Ronald Acuña Jr. did homer off of Wheeler in the third and Austin Riley smacked one out against Jonathan Bowlan in the seventh outside of those big flies (and Acuña continuing to be a thorn in Philadelphia's side), there wasn't much to cheer about from an Atlanta perspective as the Braves were unable to keep up with the Phillies on the offensive side of things.

This one was certainly looking bleak late! Once again, the Phillies rushed out to an early lead and it eventually turned into a late lead after both Derek Hill and Kyle Schwarber launched bombs at Dylan Dodd's expense to make it a 4-1 ballgame. The Braves had six outs in order to make sure that they didn't drop two in a row to Philadelphia and fortunately, they had one of their stars ready to do some more damage.

Ronald Acuña Jr. was already responsible for the lone run batted in for Atlanta up until that point (via a sacrifice fly) and he had an opportunity in the eighth inning to at least add two more RBI to his tally with both Drake Baldwin and Mike Yastrzemski in scoring position. He ended up adding three in one swing, as he turned on a 101-mph heater from Alex McFarlane and drove it into the seats in left-center for a game-changing three-run dinger (his 1,000th career hit, to boot) that brought both the Braves and the local boo-birds in Philadelphia back to life.

Jhoan Duran got the ball for the ninth inning in an effort to restore order. He did not do so, as Ozzie Albies led off the ninth with a double and then Austin Riley picked a fantastic time to hit his second triple of the season over the head of Derek Hill in center field. The three-bagger put the Braves in front, which gave Raisel Iglesias a chance to make another save. A leadoff single made things scary considering Iglesias's track record with men on base and then a productive out and a passed ball brought Stott al the way to third. For the second time in as many weeks, Iglesias ended up stranding the tying run at third base and just like that, the Braves had stolen one and guaranteed themselves the crucial road split.

Well, as you can tell by the scoreline, there wasn't much to write home about as far as the offense goes. It was always going to be tough sledding for the Braves on this particular day with Jesús Luzardo going and it ended up being the toughest sledding of all, as Luzardo ended up going the distance and pitching a complete game shutout. Atlanta only managed two hits on the day and three baserunners total, as Matt Olson and Michael Harris II got on with base knocks and then Ronald Acuña Jr. got on with a walk. That's all she wrote as far as the offense went for the Braves and it was a very, very good thing that they had the split going into this game because this would've been a very depressing note to end a four-game series loss on!

Anyways, you've got to give credit to Grant Holmes for delivering a strong performance while he was out there. Holmes went six innings and only gave up three hits and two walks while striking out six. When he left the game, it was still a scoreless tie. Instead, Didier Fuentes ended up being the "goat" in this one as he left a 2-2, 2-out pitch against Kyle Schwarber right down the middle. Schwarber is only thinking about one result and looking for one pitch in one location in that situation — he got what he wanted and that ended up being the difference!

So there you have it! Atlanta went into Philadelphia with a four-game lead in the NL East standings and they'll be leaving town with the same lead in hand. Considering the circumstances, that's a job well done for the Braves to be able to go into hostile territory with the stakes as high as they were and ultimately hold serve. It's also huge for the Braves to have gone ahead and clinched the season series over Philadelphia as well — they now hold the tiebreaker over both the team that they're pursuing for the second seed in the National League and the team that they're trying to hold off for the divisional title. It's been a productive couple of weeks for the Braves!

Perhaps the most encouraging development over the past couple of weeks is that Ronald Acuña Jr. is going back on a heater. Heading into the series finale and dating back to August 24, Acuña had been hitting .419/.458/.698 over 11 games and 48 plate appearances, good for a wOBA of .488 and a wRC+ of 213 during that short sample size. It's exactly what you want to see from a player of Acuña's caliber as the team gets closer and closer to the Postseason and hopefully this'll be the start of a special run for Acuña as the playoffs beckon.

Meanwhile, Matt Olson has been mired in a serious funk in that same span, as he's only been hitting .149/.216/.255 over the past couple of weeks with a wOBA of .205 and a wRC+ of 24. It's hard to begrudge Olson considering just how well he's been playing all season but it sure would be nice for him to figure it out at the plate as the season winds down. We're slowly but surely starting to finally see what this lineup was meant to look like when it was constructed and hopefully this team will finally start hitting on all cylinders at the plate as a unit once October rolls around.

Predictably, the pitching was solid. Chris Sale kept up his fantastic level of performance with a strong outing on Friday, Tyler Mahle pitched another six solid innings on Sunday and then Grant Holmes' six shutout innings on Monday shouldn't be forgotten, either. Martín Pérez had the only slip-up as far as starting pitching was concerned and even still, the bullpen picked up the slack and kept the Braves in that particular game. In fact, outside of stumbles from Dylan Dodd on Sunday and Didier Fuentes on Monday (and again, tough to begrudge him considering that he came up huge on Friday), the bullpen put in some really good work against Philadelphia's lineup in their own cramped ballpark.

Overall, I will absolutely take the Braves grabbing a split of this four-game series. Weirdly enough, the result may also suit the Phillies as well considering their remaining schedule. They'll be facing the Astros for the next three days while the Braves face the Rays and then after this weekend's series, Philadelphia will be taking on the Nationals for two and the Mets for four to complete their road trip before returning home to face the Brewers and the Rays. On paper, that seems imposing but both of those teams may have clinched their divisions and their Postseason seeds so they might be letting off the gas a bit in that final week.

Meanwhile, Atlanta has to take on the Rays next, then they travel to Wrigley to face a mercurial-but-tough Cubs team, then they'll be facing that same Astros team that's fighting to hold on to the AL West crown before ending the season with three at home against the Reds and three at home against the Marlins. Depending on the circumstances, both teams will have choppy seas to navigate heading into October.

The good news is that the Braves still have the four-game lead intact. That's not to say that it's a green light to let off the gas but it's still good that the Braves remain in the driver's seat. A strong homestand against the Rays and Phillies is still a must for Atlanta and with the way that they've performed at home lately, it's certainly not out of the realm of possibility that they can get it done and make sure that this lead holds up heading into mid-September. For now, Atlanta has avoided slipping up at the first hurdle and hopefully they'll continue to clear the hurdles that are ahead of them.

articles.title: Joel Klatt torches Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood: ‘Incredibly hard to watch’
articles.summary: The Michigan Wolverines football program, ever at the center of controversy, found itself involved in yet another national story after its 13-12 victory over...
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines football program, ever at the center of controversy, found itself involved in yet another national story after its 13-12 victory over the Western Michigan Broncos in Ann Arbor.

The Wolverines appeared to lose the game 12-7 after Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt went out of bounds as the clock expired on NBC's broadcast. However, the Broncos' ensuing celebration was halted when game officials, after a video review, determined that there was actually one second remaining on the Big Ten's official game clock.

In his second chance, Underwood delivered a moment that will go down in Michigan lore forever, connecting with wide receiver JJ Buchanan for a touchdown, sealing the victory for the Wolverines.

As great as the final result was for Michigan, the Wolverines shouldn't have needed one of the most controversial endings in the history of the sport and a Hail Mary attempt to beat a MAC program, and according to Fox Sports analyst Joel Klatt, a lot of Michigan's struggles can be pinned on Underwood's lackluster performance and development.

"I'm just telling you right now, guys, that the film was quite shocking," Klatt said about Underwood, who finished the game 12-for-22 with one touchdown, 170 yards, an interception, and a fumble. "I go to the first series, and I wanted to see, like, well, was it good early and then did it, did it regress late?

"And again, the film tells you a lot more than watching the game. I'm watching the game, obviously, on the airplane, and they go down the field, but what I saw on that first series Wasn't great. In fact, you look at the big completion that they got on the 2nd play of the game; that was a completely broken play after he dropped the snap. And then you get a one-handed catch and everyone's energized, and that's great. The 5th play of the game, he throws it into double coverage."

Per Klatt's analysis, things didn't improve much as the game unfolded.

"The 7th play of the game, he's RPO; he goes the wrong direction. 9Th play of the game, they were targeted wrong on a double team on the offensive line. So this is all part of their first series, and they were still able to go down there and score. So I'm thinking to myself, like, man, did it get worse? Yeah, it got worse.

"You watch the rest of the game, and I'm just telling you right now that Bryce Underwood regressed from year 1 to year 2. He's throwing curl routes into sitting safeties. He's throwing spot routes and leading those players into cover 2 corners. This is day 1 quarterback stuff. These are things that you can't do as a quarterback. And this is going to be film that is going to be incredibly hard to watch.

"For everyone on that team, because it is laid bare for everyone. It was laid bare for all of us watching. And now they're going to go in, and they're going to watch that film, and there's going to be major questions about what his status is this week going into the Oklahoma game."

Klatt wasn't the only one who took note of the young quarterback's struggles. On Monday, first-year Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham made it clear that Underwood has "to turn a corner" if he wants to hold onto the starting job. The Wolverines will host a red-hot Oklahoma Sooners team on Saturday in a game that will be closely scrutinized given how things went against the Broncos.

If Underwood can't justify Larry Ellison's massive NIL contributions to bring him into Ann Arbor, he may be on the sidelines by the time the Wolverines open conference play.

articles.title: Riley Greene and Kevin McGonigle belt home runs for Tigers in 5-4 win over Twins
articles.summary: Riley Greene had three hits, including a two-run homer, and Kevin McGonigle added a solo shot Monday to lead the Detroit Tigers to a 5-4 victory over the Min...
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — Riley Greene had three hits, including a two-run homer, and Kevin McGonigle added a solo shot Monday to lead the Detroit Tigers to a 5-4 victory over the Minnesota Twins.

Tigers starter Troy Melton (8-4) gave up four runs and seven hits in 5 2/3 innings, and four relievers held the Twins to one hit the rest of the way. Kenley Jansen pitched the ninth for his 494th career save and 18th this season.

Joe Ryan (6-9) lasted four innings for Minnesota in his return from the injured list. Trevor Larnach homered and scored twice for the Twins, who are 4 1/2 games out of a playoff spot with 18 to play.

Minnesota took a 1-0 lead in the first when Luke Keaschall scored on an RBI grounder by Ryan Jeffers.

McGonigle's 15th homer tied it in the bottom half before Detroit scored twice in the second, aided by Ryan's command issues and a throwing error by first baseman Royce Lewis. Colt Keith was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded.

Larnach launched a solo homer in the fourth, but Greene answered with a 417-foot shot off reliever Connor Prielipp in the fifth to give Detroit a 5-2 lead. Greene has six extra-base hits in his last three games.

Walker Jenkins' two-run double scored Larnach and Kaelen Culpepper to pull Minnesota to 5-4 in the sixth. The Twins loaded the bases with two outs but reliever Tyler Kinley struck out Kody Clemens.

Minnesota threatened to tie it in the eighth with Jenkins on third, but Brooks Lee flied out to end the inning.

Making his first start after missing a month with a left glute strain, Ryan allowed three runs — two earned — and three hits. He struck out seven and walked one.

Prielipp went the rest of the way and gave up two runs on five hits with five strikeouts and no walks.

Twins RHP Dean Kremer (2-5, 5.81 ERA) starts Tuesday against Tigers RHP Drew Anderson (4-5, 3.73).

This story has been corrected to show that Greene homered in the fifth inning, not the fourth.

articles.title: Falcons Recap: Stefanski sets stage for season-long QB debate
articles.summary: Kevin Stefanski's comments set stage for never-ending Falcons QB controversy
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons finally named a starting quarterback for their season opener, but somehow it still feels like there are more questions than answers surrounding the QB1 job. For now, though, the team is locked in on Sunday's season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In today's Falcons Wire Recap, Tua Tagovailoa is officially named the Week 1 starter, Michael Penix Jr. discusses his injury status, Xavier Watts gets All-Pro hype from ESPN, and Kevin Stefanski sets the stage for a season-long QB controversy.

The Falcons named Tua Tagovailoa their starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. It will be the sixth consecutive season that the Falcons roll out a different Week 1 starter at the NFL's most-prized position.

Tagovailoa completed 10 of 13 pass attempts for 117 yards over two preseason games, and while he hasn't exactly impressed in training camp, the veteran QB will look to redeem himself after losing his starting job with the Miami Dolphins last season. Hopefully, a fresh start (and a side of Bijan Robinson) is all Tua needs to turn things around.

However, Stefanski didn't exactly say that Tagovailoa won the QB competition, which leads us to our next point.

Stefanski won't commit to QB beyond Week 1

"Tua will start," Stefanski confirmed at his Monday press conference. "Cooper Rush will be the backup. Mike Penix will be inactive. Really, really proud of those guys. And I told them this morning, I think those guys have worked like crazy all offseason. They've pushed each other and supported each other."

While the Falcons may be rolling with Tagovailoa in Week 1, Stefanski did not make a definitive announcement when asked if Penix was still in the mix for the starting QB job.

"I'm gonna really stay in Week 1. I'm not going to speculate past that, I don't think it's fair to anyone at this point."

Michael Penix's comments add to QB controversy

Penix said he told Stefanski that he was not where needed to be to play in Sunday's game. And while Penix indicated he's close to being 100 percent, the third-year QB said wants to feel a little bit more confident in his knee before making his regular season debut.

"I had that conversation and I just told [Stefanski], 'I'm not where I want to be right now,'" Penix explained to reporters on Monday. "I want to be able to be 100 percent so I can help this team win football games. And I'm really close."

Even after Penix's comments, it's a little bit hard to fathom the Falcons actually leaving the decision up to their quarterback. In fact, the team seems to be going to great lengths to avoid saying anything remotely concrete regarding the quarterback position.

Stefanski initially revealed that Penix was cleared for contact immediately following QB Jack Strand's big performance against the Colts. This could have just been a coincidence, but similar to the latest Penix news, it all feels very convenient for the coaching staff.

Instead of naming either quarterback the starter, the team can point to the fact that Penix wasn't ready. It's a good strategy if you want to avoid being scrutinized in the moment, but a definitive declaration might be the better long-term move for Stefanski and the Falcons, assuming they actually want to make the playoffs this season.

ESPN predicts All-Pro team appearance for Falcons safety

Just how much better Falcons safety Xavier Watts can get is anybody's guess, but at least one analyst thinks he has All-Pro potential. Here's Seth Walder at ESPN predicting a big award for Watts at the end of the season.

"Bold prediction for 2026: Safety Xavier Watts will be a first- or second-team All-Pro. A 2025 third-round pick, Watts had an impressive rookie season in which he recorded five interceptions. If he builds on that, he'll start to be considered among the league's top safeties."

According to league insider Albert Breer at Sports Illustrated, the Falcons actually have the oldest roster in the NFL this year. If this news comes as a surprise, you're definitely not alone. The Falcons recently signed veteran edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (33 years old) and also kept 32-year-old backup Cooper Rush as one of four quarterbacks on the roster.

"Would you believe the Falcons have the NFL's oldest roster? Statistically, it's true, although it's because of a veteran offensive line that is anchored by 13-year vet Jake Matthews and guys like DE Za'Darius Smith, QB Cooper Rush and old friend TE Austin Hooper (plus kicker Nick Folk), who aren't there to play overly expansive roles." - Albert Breer , SI

articles.title: Ugly inning, twin killings cost Minnesota in 1-run loss to Tigers
articles.summary: The Twins slipped further back in the wild-card race, and time is not on their side.
articles.body:
Triple. Strikeout. Walk. Hit batter. Hit batter. Error.

That's how the Tigers scored two runs in an ugly second inning by the Twins on Monday, and it proved devastating as Detroit would go on to defeat Minnesota by a score of 5-4.

Joe Ryan, in his return from the injured list, gave up a solo homer to Rookie of the Year favorite Kevin McGonigle in the first inning, and then struggled with control in the second inning.

The All-Star right-hander gave up a triple and struck out a batter to start the second inning, and then his control vanished. Ryan walked Max Clark and then hit John Peck and Colt Keith on back-to-back pitches, the second hit batsman coming with the bases loaded.

The next batter, McGonigle, hit a grounder to Royce Lewis at first base, and Lewis threw home to catcher Ryan Jeffers. What should've been a routine force out turned into a disaster as the throw forced Jeffers to stretch to make the catch, causing his foot to drift an inch away from home plate, allowing the runner to score.

Ryan wound up striking out seven batters in four innings. He was replaced by lefty Connor Prielipp, who worked the next four innings for the Twins. Prielipp made one mistake, and it was a big one, as Riley Greene took him deep for a two-run homer in the fifth inning.

Walker Jenkins drove in two runs with a double in the sixth, cutting the Tigers' lead to one at 5-4. But Minnesota couldn't come through from there, stranding the tying runner on base in the sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth innings.

Kody Clemens struck out looking with the bases loaded to end the sixth.

Royce Lewis grounded into a double play to end the seventh.

Brooks Lee flied out with runners at the corners to end the eighth.

Josh Bell grounded into a double play to end the game.

Minnesota grounded into four double plays in the game, including once in each of the final three innings. Bell grounded into a double play to end both the first and ninth innings.

The Twins (68-76) are now eight games under .500. They remain 4 1/2 games behind Cleveland (73-71) for the final wild-card spot (the Guardians lost to Baltimore), but they're also chasing the Orioles (70-75), Rangers (71-73), and Blue Jays (72-72).

The Blue Jays had yet to play on Monday as of this writing.

Up next: Twins at Tigers, Tuesday at 5:40 p.m. CT.

articles.summary: On Monday, the Big Ten announced its Week 1 conference awards, with USC quarterback Jayden Maiava earning a notable honor
articles.body:
While there is still one college football game remaining in Week 1, the Big Ten wrapped up its first week of the season on Sunday. On Monday, the conference announced its weekly football honors .

This marks the second weekly honor of the season for Maiava. Last week, he was named the Associated Press national player of the week for Week 0, in which USC defeated San Jose State 42-26.

articles.title: Giants release WR Darius Slayton who signed $36 million deal in 2025
articles.summary: The New York Giants have released wide receiver Darius Slayton, whom they just signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in March of 2025.
articles.body:
The New York Giants have released wide receiver Darius Slayton, who has been with the team since being drafted in the fifth round in 2019. He just signed a three-year, $36 million contract with New York in March of 2025.

In his time with the Giants, Slayton played in a total of 106 games, starting 78 of those, with 296 receptions for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns. Last season, he had a career-low in touchdowns with only one despite playing 81 percent of the offensive snaps in 14 games. Slayton also had only 37 receptions for 538 yards, his fewest since 2021, when he started only five games.

During the past two years, Slayton's production has been steadily declining after reaching over 700 receiving yards in 2022 and 2023. With his numbers declining, he was arguably no longer worth his nearly $16 million cap hit this season, especially after signing quarterback Jameis Winston and guard Joe Runyan to contract extensions.

With Slayton no longer on the roster, the Giants have Darnell Mooney, Odell Beckham Jr and rookie Malachi Fields behind their No. 1 wide receiver, Malik Nabers.

Beckham Jr. has not played in an NFL game since his brief time with the Miami Dolphins in 2024, when he had 9 receptions for 55 yards over 9 games. However, he earned a spot on the active roster through his performance in training camp. New York also has Braxton Berrios on the practice squad for extra receiver depth.

articles.title: Who is ranked too high, too low on ESPN’s Week 2 college football FPI?
articles.summary: ESPN's updated college football FPI has some surprising rankings entering Week 2, including teams that may be ranked too high and others deserving of more re...
articles.body:
The college football season is officially in full swing following Week 1. There were a number of hot starts, controversies and Heisman-worthy performances.

On Monday, ESPN released its updated college football FPI heading toward Week 2. There were some interesting observations from the analytics machine.

There are a few teams whose hype may be a bit ahead of reality and some that aren't getting enough love. Here are the teams ranked too high and too low in this installment of ESPN's college football FPI.

Sep 5, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns edge Colin Simmons (1) reacts after recovering a fumble during the third quarter against the Texas State Bobcats at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Let's pump the brakes on the Texas Longhorns. Yes, they had a huge, lopsided win on Saturday against … Texas State. They were No. 2 in the preseason ESPN FPI, and they probably should still be there.

The Longhorns will have a chance to prove their new ranking right on Saturday. The Longhorns welcome the previous FPI No. 1 Ohio State to Austin, Texas, for a monster showdown.

Until they beat a College Football Playoff contender like Ohio State, it doesn't matter what the analytics say. They aren't No. 1 until they prove it. Saturday is the big opportunity for head coach Steve Sarkisian's team.

Sep 4, 2026; Stanford, California, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) runs after the catch for a touchdown against the Stanford Cardinal during the third quarter at Stanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Miami, ranked No. 4, is probably the second- or third-best team in the nation. The Hurricanes have an outstanding receiver in Malachi Toney, a loaded defense, and a quarterback who could hear his name called very early next April.

The biggest question for Miami is handling expectations following a deep playoff run. If Saturday's performance against an ACC foe was any indication, things are being handled well.

Miami is a legitimate contender that might be a few steps better than last year's team.

Sep 5, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; Michigan Wolverines running back Bryson Kuzdzal (24) fumbles the ball while being tackled by Western Michigan cornerback Jordon Thomas (13) in the third quarter at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Let's all be honest here. Michigan should not have won on Saturday. The more you look at the replay, the more obvious it is that time ran out. The "hidden clock" is completely baffling to process as an actual explanation.

Michigan shouldn't be in the top 25. They just shouldn't. Regardless of the talent on this team, Saturday's performance was not worthy of a top-25 ranking.

It's honestly very puzzling that ESPN's FPI has them ranked No. 20.

Aug 29, 2026; Charlottesville, Virginia, USA; Virginia Cavaliers running back Noah Vaughn (3) rushes the ball during the game against the North Carolina State Wolfpack at Scott Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

If any team should be ranked ahead of Michigan, it is Virginia. The Cavaliers took on NC State in Week 0 and completely tore them apart. This NC State team was projected to be one of its best versions in years.

Virginia dominated them and didn't apologize. To be ranked No. 25 after shredding an ACC foe, well behind Michigan of all teams, is really puzzling.

articles.title: Lakers Face Growing ‘Bronny James Problem’ After LeBron Departure
articles.summary: LeBron James leaving is just one of many reasons why his son, Bronny James, has a growing uncertain future playing for the Los Angeles Lakers. The post Laker...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers underwent major roster changes over the 2026 NBA offseason, which included the departure of LeBron James and the addition of new players who fit around franchise star Luka Doncic. But despite all the big changes, Bronny James remains on the roster, now with a guaranteed contract for next season, which, according to one Lakers writer, could become a 'problem' for the team in the upcoming year.

The younger James has been the subject of controversy since he was selected by Los Angeles with the 54th pick of the 2024 NBA Draft, and while he has yet to become a consistent contributor through his first two seasons in the league, remains one of the most well-known names on the current roster.

With that, questions continue about James' fit on the team next to Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, and all the other players the Lakers' front office added this summer. As time goes on, the pressure on him is mounting, and now no longer on the same team as his father, Bronny could be facing a huge uphill battle in 2026-27 to prove himself as an NBA-caliber player.

Lakers Could Start Facing A 'Bronny James Problem'

Writing for LakeShowLife.com , Tyler Watts believes James will struggle to get consistent minutes in what is the biggest 'prove it' season of his career.

In his recent article, the Lakers writer said that, specifically, the addition of Collin Sexton in free agency makes it a lot more difficult for James to crack head coach JJ Redick's rotation on a nightly basis.

"LA signed Collin Sexton to a two-year, $19.2 million contract this offseason to be their sixth man. Sexton is a score-first guard with serious defensive issues . Head coach JJ Redick can't play Bronny alongside him, leaving LeBron's son without a role," he wrote.

In his rookie season, James averaged 2.3 points, 0.7 rebounds, and 0.8 assists on 31.3% shooting. He had a slightly better second year with averages of 2.9 points, 0.5 rebounds, and 1.2 assists on 40.9% shooting in 42 games, but he has yet to carve out a role for himself as an undersized guard on a team full of backcourt talent.

The Lakers have a ton of wing and guard talent, meaning James has fallen down the depth chart after all the offseason additions. As Watts explained, right when the young player needs to prove his value the most, he's likely going to have the least amount of opportunity to do so.

"The Los Angeles Lakers have a Bronny James problem. He must prove he is ready to be in the nightly rotation, but Bronny doesn't fit next to Collin Sexton. He isn't ready to be in the starting five, so it will take a significant leap for James to get minutes. Crazier things have happened, but it feels like Bronny will be glued to the bench again, waiting for an opportunity when someone misses time."

A Bronny James-related problem could also be compounded with the Lakers, a team already filled with drama, considering his name and family ties. If Redick isn't playing him, fans and the media will be asking questions, a lot more than would come compared to if they picked someone else late in the second round back in 2024.

Have the Lakers put themselves in a tough situation by guaranteeing James' contract just before his father left town? Potentially. But regardless, that's the situation both sides are in now, and things could get worse for the Lakers and James as the season goes on.

Make-Or-Break Year For LeBron James' Son In Los Angeles

With all that said, in a separate article , Watts explained how James' future with the Lakers is more up in the air than ever before heading into the 2026-27 NBA season.

"Bronny James is a player without a position. He is too small to be a two and doesn't have the playmaking chops to thrive as a point guard," he wrote. "His lack of a true role and position has made it difficult for coach Redick to find consistent minutes for James. Bronny has never appeared in more than 42 games in a season and has yet to average more than 8.9 minutes per contest."

Los Angeles currently has 16 players on the roster. They will need to cut that number down to 15 by October 1, meaning there is a realistic chance James is cut or waived before the season, despite his guaranteed contract and name recognition across the sports world.

"The Lakers must quickly figure it out. Bronny has to improve and cement himself in the rotation. Redick gave him the blueprint, but James isn't following it," he added. "Bronny has an opportunity. That is all fans can ask for after his first two years. Now it is on the guard to adapt, or it will be time for the purple and gold to move on."

Bronny James has shown massive potential during his stints in the G-League. However, that has yet to translate to the NBA level.

It will be difficult for the 22-year-old to prove his value with the Lakers this season, but in the limited on-court action he'll likely see this year, he'll have to do everything he can to prove his worth and either stick around in Los Angeles or find his way onto another roster.

On Monday afternoon, the San Diego Padres will face off against the Washington Nationals at Petco Park.

Catcher Luis Campusano went 2-for-3 with a home run in the win on Sunday.

Ahead of the series opener against the Nationals, the San Diego Padres have announced their starting lineup.

Underdog MLB posted on X: "Padres 9/7 F. Tatis Jr. RF J. Cronenworth 2B M. Machado 3B T. France 1B J. Merrill CF L. Campusano DH D. Harris LF X. Bogaerts SS E. Salas C N. Pivetta SP" After his impressive series, which featured two home runs while also playing strong defense as the team's catcher, against the Yankees, Luis Campusano will serve as the team's designated hitter. Meanwhile, San Diego's top prospect Ethan Salas will get his second start at catcher since being called up.

Campusano started as the team's designated hitter during the team's 5-1 loss on Saturday. He went 0-for-3 with a walk. Monday's game will mark the seventh time Campusano has appeared as a designated hitter for the Padres this season. In his previous six appearances, Campusano has a 98 WRC+. As a catcher, Campusano's WRC+ is 154.

Overall, Campusano is batting .285 with 47 hits, 11 doubles, seven home runs, 20 runs, 26 RBIs and 25 walks in 58 games.

After winning two out of three against the Yankees, the San Diego Padres improved to 75-68. The Padres have gone 4-6 over their last 10 games. San Diego is currently 0.5 games behind the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third Wild Card berth in the National League.

Monday's game will feature the return of right-handed pitcher Nick Pivetta. Pivetta has missed most of the season with an elbow injury he suffered during his fourth start this year. Last season, Pivetta had a 13-5 record with a 2.87 ERA in 181.2 innings.

Meanwhile at 67-78, the Washington Nationals have fallen out of the playoff race. Washington has gone 5-5 over their last 10 games.

Right-hander Jake Irvin is expected to start for the Nationals on Monday. It will mark Irvin's 19th start this season. Irvin has a 2-8 record and a 5.57 ERA in 85.2 innings.
