articles.title: Ohtani back in Dodger lineup for Reds, who add Ke'Bryan Hayes
articles.summary: Four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani returns to the Dodgers lineup after missing 4 games because of knee soreness. The Reds activated Ke'Bryan Hayes from IL.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- As the Cincinnati Reds returned to Dodger Stadium for the first time since last year's brief playoff appearance, they got a player back to help their lineup.

Problem for the Reds : So did the Dodgers.

The Reds activated light-hitting, Gold Glove third baseman Ke'Bryan Hayes after 11 days on the injured list for a left groin strain.

The Dodgers, meanwhile, returned all-time baseball unicorn Shohei Ohtani to their lineup for this week's series opener Monday (Sept. 7) after Ohtani had missed the previous four games because of knee soreness.

The Reds, who remain in last place in the NL Central despite winning their last three series against teams in playoff position (7-3 in their last 10 games entering the week), face the Dodgers in seven of the next 10 games, with three against the MLB-best Brewers in Milwaukee wedged in the middle of that stretch.

The Dodgers, who have the second-best record in the majors as they make a bid for a third consecutive World Series championship, are in position to clinched the NL West during that stretch.

He played for the Reds!? Do you remember these players' time in Cincy?

The Reds optioned infielder Edwin Arroyo back to Triple-A Louisville as the corresponding move for Hayes. Arroyo had only one hit in 17 at-bats in his latest call-up.

images.caption: Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart (27) embraces Cincinnati Reds infielder Edwin Arroyo (2) while reacting to the Cincinnati Reds defeating San Diego Padres in the MLB game at Great American Ball Park in Cincinnati on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

Being the oldest pro baseball team means lots of players have made their way through Cincinnati. Take a look at these guys, who were more famous elsewhere, but wore a Reds uniform. (The Enquirer/ Amanda Rossmann)

Hall-of-Famer Christy Mathewson won 373 career game - 372 with the New York Giants. His other win came in the only game he pitched for the Reds in 1916. (From the George Grantham Bain Collection at the Library of Congress)

Don Newcombe was a four-time all-star, a Rookie of the Year and was the 1956 NL MVP and Cy Young award winner with the Dodgers. He pitched in 66 games for the Reds from 1958-1960. (The Enquirer/Carl Wellinger)

Billy Martin won four World Series as a player for the New York Yankees before going on to even greater fame as a manager, including a 1977 World Series championship. He spent 1960 in Cincinnati where he hit .246 in 103 games for the Reds. (The Enquirer/Herb Heise)

Roger Craig (37) managed the San Francisco Giants from 1985-92, including a World Series appearance in 1989. He spent 12 seasons as a pitcher in the majors, including 40 games for the Reds in 1965. (The Enquirer/Herb Heise)

Charlie Leibrandt won 140 games over a 14-year MLB career, including memorable stints with the Kansas City Royals and Atlanta Braves. He got his start in Cincinnati, throwing 82 games for the Reds from 1979-82. (The Enquirer/Fred Straub)
César Cedeño was a four-time all-star and won five Gold Gloves with the Houston Astros in the 1970s. He played 429 games for the Reds from 1982-85. (The Enquirer/Dick Swaim)

articles.title: Red Bull keeps Lawson for Madrid GP as Hadjar’s wrist recovery drags on
articles.summary: For a third consecutive race, Liam Lawson will join Max Verstappen as a Red Bull driver while Isack Hadjar recovers from a broken wrist, the Formula 1 team a...
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — For a third consecutive race, Liam Lawson will join Max Verstappen as a Red Bull driver while Isack Hadjar recovers from a broken wrist , the Formula 1 team announced on Monday.

Hadjar was injured during the summer break and still has not fully recovered, leading Red Bull to let Lawson drive in the Madrid Grand Prix this week.

"Isack's recovery continues to progress positively. While he is not ready to return to the cockpit he will be in Madrid supporting the team," Red Bull said in a statement.

Lawson is having his strongest season in F1 and is ninth in the standings, one place behind Hadjar. That's helped bring about the New Zealander's return to Red Bull, where he was dropped after just two races in 2025.

"Everyone at Oracle Red Bull Racing looks forward to welcome Isack back behind the wheel very soon," the team added.

After the Madrid GP, the series goes to Azerbaijan on Sept. 26.

articles.title: MarShawn Lloyd sends strong message to league ahead of taking Packers backfield
articles.summary: The USC product is ready for people to learn his name.
articles.body:
Green Bay's backfield has a new sheriff.

With Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List, the Packers will be without their typical starter for now.

That means MarShawn Lloyd, a third year rusher out of USC, is taking over.

Lloyd has played in just one game since joining the NFL. He was a great player in college but is unproven at the highest level.

He had a message to share with fans and opponents ahead of his debut as a starter.

MarShawn Lloyd sends message ahead of week 1

It's MarShawn Lloyd's first week of practice as the go-to for Green Bay and he had a message to put out.

"A lot of players don't know me. They'll watch my college tape, if anything. They won't even know anything about me, won't even worry about me. But they will eventually at some point this year," Lloyd said as reported by NBC 26's Kelly Hallinan .

Lloyd, who has a handful of NFL snaps under his belt, said what everyone was thinking.

He's an unknown commodity. A player who once had high stock but has yet to prove it.

In three years at USC, Lloyd racked up 1,621 rushing yards and 18 TD's. In the NFL? He's got 15 total yards.

What Lloyd did pledge was that he will become a reliable option at running back. He says those player who don't know him now, "will eventually" know him.

It's a strong message spoken behind a curtain of subtlety.

For fans of the Packers and Lloyd this is great news.

articles.title: Jacoby Brissett among Cardinals' team captains
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett who is in his first season as a starter for the Cardinals, was named one of five captains for the team this season.
articles.body:
Jacoby Brissett who is in his first season as a starter for the Cardinals, was named one of five captains for the team this season.

On Monday, the Cardinals announced results of the players' captainship vote from Thursday.

Center Hjalte Froholdt was the other offensive captain. Safety Budda Baker and linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. were the defensive captains. Long snapper Casey Kreiter will represent the special teams.

"Whether you are a captain or not a captain, you be who you are within your own personality," coach Mike LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website. "When you do get voted a captain, that says your teammates and the locker room looks up to you.

"I can't think of five better people to look up to, in terms of guys who will keep it real with each other, hold people to standards, communicate with me. I don't need to know everything that's going on in the locker room. I just need to know what's pertinent."

It is the fifth consecutive season for Baker to serve as a captain. Froholdt and Wilson are repeat picks, after becoming captains for the first time in their careers last year.

"There were quite a few guys who I won't mention who were right up there in the running for it," LaFleur said. "These guys are still going to have a voice, too. And some of it will be through the silent tape, if that makes sense. That's as important as anything, actually what you're doing [on the field]."

articles.title: Texas Gets Bad News Ahead of Massive Battle Against Ohio State
articles.summary: No. 5 Texas will play one of the biggest games of the college football regular season this coming Saturday when No. 1 Ohio State comes to town.Arch Manning a...
articles.body:
No. 5 Texas will play one of the biggest games of the college football regular season this coming Saturday when No. 1 Ohio State comes to town.

Arch Manning and the Longhorns dominated Texas State 59-7, while Jeremiah Smith erupted for the Buckeyes in a 56-3 win against Ball State.

However, Texas will be without one of its skill players in running back Derrek Cooper. The freshman sustained an ankle injury in the second quarter of Saturday's win, and head coach Steve Sarkisian announced that he will be in a boot for the foreseeable future.

He carried the ball twice for six yards before his injury.

Cooper won't take the field against the Buckeyes, and it's unknown when he will return.

Cooper was a four-star recruit out of high school, per 247Sports. The Longhorns listed Cooper as the third option on the depth chart at running back, behind stars Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown.

It was unlikely Cooper would get a ton of reps this season behind that pair, but he seemed to be a reliable backup plan if one of the two went down with an injury.

In what is maybe the biggest game of the regular season, Jeremiah Smith and the Buckeyes head to Texas to play Arch Manning and the Longhorns.

Arch looked a lot more crisp in the season opener, throwing 20/27 for 305 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. His incredible wide receiver pair in Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman provide a lot of help.

Julian Sayin was excellent too, throwing 21/25 for 320 yards and three touchdowns. It'll be a battle all over the field, especially at the quarterback position between two of the country's best.

Jeremiah Smith is trying to cement himself in the Heisman race, catching the ball eight times for 151 yards and two touchdowns — in the first half. Smith will have a tougher test this week, and will look to have a better output than he did against the Longhorns last season.

articles.title: Steelers head coach says quiet part out loud about previously injured rookie
articles.summary: The Steelers likely won't be giving one rookie the starting nod in Week 1, as Mike McCarthy said the quiet part out loud about a previous injury.
articles.body:
There's an offensive position where the Pittsburgh Steelers have yet to name a starter, but Mike McCarthy just said the quiet part out loud about why it likely won't be a previously injured rookie.

Speaking with reporters on Monday, McCarthy shared the ugly truth about Max Iheanachor's missed time due to injury, pointing out that it may be tough to throw him into a starting role early.

"Well, I mean, he's an injured player," McCarthy said about Iheanachor. "You have injured players miss games because of injuries, business situations or whatever the criteria is," McCarthy said. "Availability and accountability are the most important parts of this, and being available every single day is huge, especially if you're a rookie. There's so much to love about Max just in the time he's been out there. It's impressive. Make no doubt about that, he can play. But he hasn't played."

Although McCarthy declined to declare a definitive starter for Week 1, he admitted that Dylan Cook has been getting "most of the reps" as the first-team right tackle.

Considering McCarthy's comments on both Iheanachor and Cook, it's fair to guess that the latter will get the starting nod in Week 1, even if the Steelers aren't ready to admit it quite yet.

articles.title: Kyle Schwarber Makes Phillies History in Win Over Braves
articles.summary: All-Star slugger Kyle Schwarber made history in the Philadelphia Phillies‘ 1-0 win over the Atlanta Braves. His game-winning home run in the eighth inning wa...
articles.body:
All-Star slugger Kyle Schwarber made history in the Philadelphia Phillies' 1-0 win over the Atlanta Braves. His game-winning home run in the eighth inning was the 230th as a Phillie.

That breaks Ryan Howard's record for most home runs over a five-year span with the franchise. Howard's best five-year run with the long ball came from 2006-2010. He slugged 229 home runs over that stretch, helping the Phillies win a championship in 2008.

The Phillies originally signed Kyle Schwarber to a four-year, $79 million deal ahead of the 2022 season. That's a deal that aged very well for the team over its duration. Schwarber finished second in last year's MVP race after hitting a National League-leading 56 home runs.

He re-signed with the club on a five-year, $150 million deal to reprise his role as the team's top power threat. Schwarber is on track to repeat as the NL's home run champion.

In his five seasons with the Phillies, Schwarber has launched at least 38 home runs. He's crushed at least 40 in four of his five seasons in Philadelphia. It makes sense, since Citizens Bank Park has the highest three-year rolling park factor on left-handed home runs, according to Statcast .

Kyle Schwarber Chases Babe Ruth Home Run Record

There is still one more record for Schwarber to chase: most home runs in his first five years with a new team. He's still five home runs shy of Babe Ruth's 1919-1923 home run total with the New York Yankees , according to MLB's Sarah Langs .

Schwarber has 18 games to try to pass the Babe on that list. He's currently on a hot streak, slugging home runs in three consecutive games against the Braves.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili Results, Highlights: Taylor Ends Legendary Career With a Win at Croke Park

articles.body:
Katie Taylor finally got a chance to compete at Croke Park, ending her career with a win at the historic venue in front of family and friends.

Taylor beat Flora Pili via unanimous decision to become an undisputed champion for a third time. It's her second time holding all the gold at super lightweight. The scores read 100-90, 100-90, 98-91.

Over 80,000 fans filled Croke Park, the legendary venue that last held a boxing event in 1972, when Muhammad Ali beat Al Lewis. Their voices were heard through fight night. The entrance was an emotional one. Eddie Hearn, with her since day one, was a wreck. When Taylor entered the ring, there was not a dry eye in the house.

Taylor (26-1) was electric from the start, looking looser than ever before. She landed several jabs and inside body shots, backing up when she needed to. Pili (12-1) had her hands down at several points.

Though she looked frozen in the moment, Pili had a great seventh round. It was her best effort. Taylor, who kept her emotions in check until the final bell, pushed Pili back with several jabs and hooks. Taylor's power shots were key in getting the win.

The last minute of the fight had the fans on their feet, and in the final 10 seconds, with Taylor landing flurries, the crowd gave her a standing ovation. Then the party began as "Celebration" blasted through the speakers.

After the fight, an emotional Hearn let Taylor be alone in the ring, soaking it all in. She put her gloves in the middle of the ring along with all her titles. It was a fairytale ending for a true trailblazer.

Taylor ends her career on a four-fight win streak. "The Bray Bomber" has beaten the best boxing has to offer. She's been watched by millions, brought new eyes to the sport, and changed the game for women's boxing and Ireland. And now she rides off into the sunset with gold and plenty of adulation.

articles.title: Rybakina sweeps past Osaka to close in on number one ranking
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina sweeps aside two-time champion Naomi Osaka to reach the US Open quarter-finals and close in on becoming world number one.
articles.body:
Elena Rybakina swept aside two-time champion Naomi Osaka to reach the quarter-finals of the US Open and close in on becoming world number one.

The Kazakh second seed overpowered 13th seed Osaka to win 6-1 6-4 on Louis Armstrong Stadium to set up a quarter-final against China's Zheng Qinwen.

Rybakina will become world number one for the first time if she wins her last-eight tie in New York - even if top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka goes on to defend her title.

Reigning Olympic champion Zheng came from 5-0 down in the first set of her fourth-round match to beat former champion Iga Swiatek.

"Of course I want it, I don't know anyone who won't want this," Rybakina said of the number one ranking.

"I tried to approach it the same way and do everything I can, and fight to the end of my next match.

"If I serve as well as I did today, I think I can do well. Let's hope it goes my way."

Rybakina, 27, dropped only four points in a near flawless performance on serve against four-time Grand Slam champion Osaka.

She faced the 28-year-old full of confidence, having not dropped a set in her opening three matches at the tournament, and took control of the contest in a dominant first set.

Reigning Australian Open champion Rybakina opened up a double break over Osaka, before sealing the set in just 21 minutes.

Osaka showed greater resistance early in the second set but, after failing to convert her only break point of the match, Rybakina soon seized control again.

She broke to go 4-3 up, before safely seeing out the rest of the match, with Osaka unable to contend with her opponent's deep groundstrokes.

Rybakina sealed the match inside 66 minutes with her seventh ace of a match where she hit a total of 29 winners to Osaka's nine.

articles.title: Titans defense takes major Hit ahead of season opener against Jets
articles.summary: Titans linebacker Cedric Gray’s Week 1 status is uncertain after a UTV accident left the team’s leading tackler in concussion protocol just days before the s...
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans could be without one of their most productive defensive players when they begin the 2026 NFL season.

Linebacker Cedric Gray has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after being involved in a UTV accident over the weekend in Tennessee, the team announced Monday.

According to the Titans, Gray was driving the vehicle when the accident occurred and suffered a concussion along with other minor injuries. A team source told ESPN that alcohol and reckless driving were not factors in the incident.

While the injuries were described as minor outside of the concussion, Gray's availability for Tennessee's Week 1 matchup against the New York Jets is now uncertain.

The Titans are scheduled to host the Jets on Sunday at Nissan Stadium.

Before Gray can return to the field, he must complete the NFL's required concussion protocol. The process includes several stages designed to determine whether a player can safely resume football activities.

Gray injury could shake up Titans defense before Jets game

Gray will also have to be evaluated by an independent neurological consultant. He can only be cleared to play once the consultant and Tennessee's team physician agree that his concussion symptoms have been resolved.

The Titans expressed optimism about Gray's recovery while making it clear his health will come first.

"We look forward to Cedric returning to the field soon and in full health when he clears the NFL's concussion protocol," the organization said in a statement.

Gray's potential absence would be significant for Tennessee's defense.

The linebacker emerged as one of the team's most productive defenders last season, starting 16 games and leading the Titans with 164 tackles. His ability to consistently find the football made him an important part of Tennessee's defensive unit heading into 2026.

There is still an opportunity for Gray to complete the protocol and receive clearance before Sunday's opener.

For now, however, his status remains uncertain.

With the Jets coming to Nashville and Week 1 quickly approaching, Gray's progress through concussion protocol will be one of the biggest situations for the Titans to monitor throughout the week.

articles.title: Tigers 5, Twins 4: Rookies shine, vets struggle on Labor Day
articles.summary: Killer double plays, bad defense, and bad execution, a tale as old as time. But at least the kids looked good!
articles.body:
It was a labor of a game on Labor Day. The Twins were resilient and had plenty of chances to score, but more bad luck with RISP, four double plays, and poor defensive execution led to another Twins loss. The same script as most of the second half.

The Twins once again struck first in the game. Luke Keaschall was hit by a pitch and Brooks Lee stroked a strong single to center. Keaschall and Lee then double stole to put two in scoring position for the heart of the lineup. Kody Clemens struck out and Ryan Jeffers hit into a fielders choice, scoring one and keeping runners at the corners with only one out, but Josh Bell hit into a double play to end the inning.

Joe Ryan made his grand return and was reasonably effective. After only one short rehab appearance, the Twins limited his workload to 65 pitches with rookie left-hander Connor Prielipp scheduled to follow. Ryan had a long first two innings, throwing 43 pitches and allowing three runs, but it genuinely could have been much worse.

Ryan K'd Colt Keith on three pitches to start the inning, but left a heater down the heart of the plate to AL ROY favorite Kevin McGonigle, giving Detroit their first run. In the second, he gave up a leadoff triple and struck out Spencer Torkelson, and then had perhaps the worst 4 pitch sequence of his life. Ryan walked rookie Max Clark after a long battle, then hit light-hitting rookie John Peck on the very next pitch to load the bases. On the next pitch he hit Keith to plate the go-ahead run, and then McGonigle reached on a soft grounder to first, but Royce Lewis' throw home took Jeffers off the plate and allowed the Tigers to score another. Ryan buckled in and got the next two Tigers to end the threat, but the damage was done.

Ryan locked in from there, retiring the next six straight Tigers batters, including three strikeouts, to end his day at four innings and 66 pitches. It was a decent return for the Twins' ace. His velocity looked strong and other than the McGongile homer (the only hard hit ball he allowed), he pitched reasonably well for someone effectively making his second rehab appearance. Some better defense behind him and he likely puts the Twins in a great position to win.

Connor Prielipp took over from there and was also pretty strong the rest of the way. He gave up a two-run shot to All-Star Riley Greene, but gave the Twins four strong and efficient innings and continues to show good stuff despite being 40 innings over his 2025 career high and flying past the combined 58 innings he threw from 2020-2024. The numbers won't dazzle you, but he's done more than enough to warrant a 2027 rotation look and stave off the bullpen concerns some evaluators thought he was destined for.

Back on the offensive side, the Twins did an excellent job getting back in the game after falling behind. Trevor Larnach, who has been hearing the call of the void, shrunk the gap to 1 with a laser wall-scraper in the fourth. Then, they finally managed to string some hits together with two outs in the sixth, trailing 5-2 at this point. Larnach got things started again with a single and Kaelen Culpepper scorched a single to left on the next pitch. Walker Jenkins then had his best at-bat as a Twin so far, working a full count before scorching a double into the right-center gap to plate two. If it wasn't for Tigers centerfielder Max Clark's speed, Jenkins might have had an inside-the-park home run in cavernous C0merica Park, but Clark made a nifty play, sliding to cut off the ball in the gap before it could get past him.

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video .

Twins legend Tyler Kinley came in to try to finish the game, but walked Keaschall and Lee to juice the bases for Clemens, who watched a fastball down the middle of the plate to end the threat with the Twins trailing 5-4. They had chances in every inning that followed, but hit into double plays in each of the final three frames to stop any momentum they had built.

Minnesota had one final chance to pull out a win in the ninth, but once again couldn't come up with the final hit they needed. A leadoff walk to Clemens put the tying run on. Jeffers then hit a fly ball about 400 feet out to dead center that stayed in the park and Josh Bell bounced into a double play to end the game.

They "only" left 10 men on base this game, which doesn't seem that bad, but that's because double plays don't count for that number. They had at least one runner reach base in every inning and two runners in five of them, yet only managed three total runs in those innings with multiple baserunners. Little things like that are what has the Twins well outside the playoff field with three weeks to go.

Bottom of the lineup (Larnach/Kreidler, Culpepper, Jenkins): 5-10, HR, 2B, BB, 3 RBI

Luke Keaschall: 1-2, 2 BB, stole third base

Rest of the lineup: 2-20, 3 BB, 3 GIDP, 0-6 with RISP

We're back tomorrow for the stellar pitching matchup of Dean Kremer vs Drew Anderson, which we've all been waiting for. Here's hoping Emmanuel Rodriguez and Alan Roden are with the team, too!

articles.title: ‘You definitely want to show well for the conference’: Early test vs. Arkansas important for Utes and Big 12
articles.summary: The Razorbacks will make the trip to Salt Lake City, marking just the second time an SEC opponent has visited Rice-Eccles Stadium.
articles.body:
After a game against Idaho that allowed the Utes to ease into the season a bit and test out their depth , the real season starts on Saturday with a late-night contest against Arkansas.

The Razorbacks will make the trip to Salt Lake City, marking just the second time an SEC opponent has visited Rice-Eccles Stadium. For the Utes, it's the first test they've faced this season, but it's also an opportunity to earn the Big 12 Conference some bragging rights with a win over an SEC team.

"You definitely want to show well for the conference. Just the challenge of playing top-quality teams — regardless of where they're coming from, you want to be able to show your best stuff," said Utah coach Morgan Scalley.

"Arkansas has a long history of great football, so we're excited to host and, yes, we want to represent the Big 12. We want to represent the state of Utah the right way, and our boys are getting ready for that."

Utah had an easy 66-14 win over FCS opponent Idaho to open the season, but Arkansas — picked to finish last in the SEC — didn't fare as well in its opening win over FCS North Alabama.

Though the Razorbacks won 31-14 and gained 415 yards, Arkansas coach Ryan Silverfield called it "one of the worst offensive performances that I've been a part of."

Arkansas gained only 148 rushing yards and its offensive line graded out poorly, allowing three sacks and five tackles for loss. Starting quarterback KJ Jackson threw for 267 yards and three touchdowns, but also threw an interception and lost a fumble.

Arkansas' defense had a good showing, holding the Lions to 153 yards of total offense and only 40 yards of rushing. At halftime, North Alabama had just 18 yards of offense. Arkansas finished with two sacks, five tackles for loss and a recovered fumble.

The Hogs' defensive line will provide the Utes' new-look offensive line with its first big test of the season.

"You watch that team and they're big, big up front. So that's, again, going to be the challenge is that battle up front, both on the offense and defensive sides. They've got a very twitchy athletic edge rusher in (Steven Soles Jr.), who is a transfer from Kentucky. They're more of an odd front with (defensive coordinator) Ron Roberts coming from Florida," Scalley said.

Utah was missing projected offensive line starter Keith Olson and projected rotation player Isaiah Garcia to begin the season, starting Zereoue Williams, Solatoa Moea'i, Alex Harrison, Roger Alderman and Cedric Jefferson. For the most part, the group was solid, but — as expected — took a little bit to get going.

"I felt as the game went on, they played much more cohesive … Didn't give up a sack, proud of the way our offensive line (played). We had a good rotation there at the guard spot. I thought guys got quality reps, and so we'll settle in on a starting five this week that hopefully can last us throughout the game," Scalley said.

Though Dampier got hit more than Utah wanted at the start of the game, it wasn't all on the offensive line, Scalley said.

"To Devon getting hit, some of that was him — pulling the ball, holding onto the ball for a little bit. Sometimes those options when you're doing the read fakes and stuff like that, you're going to end up getting your quarterback hit at times, but we'd like to definitely take those hits off of him. We don't want him getting hit as much as he was getting hit early in that game," Scalley said.

The Razorbacks' offense was not overly impressive in Week 1, but things can change drastically from week to week in college football. The Utes' defensive line will be challenged by an Arkansas offensive front that has things to work on, but poses a much bigger threat than Idaho.

"On the offensive side of the ball, very stout up front," Scalley said.

Utah rotated early and often on the defensive line in Thursday's opener, doing a full-scale line change as soon as Idaho's third drive. The Utes started with Lance Holtzclaw, Karson Kaufusi, Jireh Moe and Ethan Day, and that's who Ute fans should expect to see on Saturday night.

Holtzclaw, Kaufusi, Moe and Day were ranked in the top seven of Utah's best-performing defensive players on Thursday, per Pro Football Focus.

"Really felt good about Karson Kaufusi. I thought he played very well. Jireh Moe did some really good things and then I thought Lance Holtzclaw was all over the field providing pressure," Scalley said. "A lot of QB hits in that game, which is kind of what we're after, is making him throw off-schedule, making him uncomfortable. So there are definitely some things to clean up, but overall happy."

Running back Daniel Bray, who is expected to see a lot of time this season behind RB1 Wayshawn Parker, played just three snaps and rushed for 13 yards before suffering an early injury that took him out of the rest of the game.

Scalley said Bray suffered a concussion.

"He's going through the protocol right now. It looks like we're on track to have him back, but with concussions, you never know day to day how they handle everything. So we're making sure that he's safe and ready to go," Scalley said.

articles.title: Evansville women's basketball player, former Castle standout, dies in car crash
articles.summary: The University of Evansville, Wabash Valley College and Castle High School announced the death of basketball player Jordan Scott.
articles.body:
EVANSVILLE — University of Evansville women's basketball player Jordan Scott has died.

UE officials confirmed the Castle High School graduate died following a car wreck on Sunday, Sept. 6. Scott joined the Purple Aces this offseason as part of coach Ben Wierzba's first recruiting class.

The following statement was sent to the Courier & Press, part of the USA TODAY Network.

"There is no simple way to put it, but our team and coaches are really struggling," Wierzba said. "While this is a new team and we have only been together for a short time, these young women have spent countless hours together this summer and fall building something special, and they have quickly become a family. Jordan was a meaningful part of the family, and her presence, personality, and spirit made an impact on all of us. Our hearts our broken for her family and especially for Jayden. Jordan will always be a part of the Evansville Women's Basketball Program."

Details about the wreck weren't immediately available from local law enforcement officials.

Scott started multiple years at Castle under former coach Bobby Meier. The 5-foot-6 point guard averaged double figures her final three years with the Knights and was twice chosen First Team All-Southern Indiana Athletic Conferece. She played 16 games on the 2022 sectional champion team as a freshman.

Castle administration sent the following statement:

"It is with a heavy heart and profound sadness that the Castle High School family acknowledges the tragic passing of Jordan Scott, a cherished member of our Class of 2025. During her time at Castle, Jordan was a vibrant presence both in our hallways and on the basketball court. As a standout player for our girls basketball team, she exemplified dedication, leadership, and a fierce competitive spirit that inspired her teammates, coaches, and the entire Knight community.

"Jordan was continuing her academic and athletic journey this year at University of Evansville after one year at Wabash Valley College, and we remain incredibly proud to call her one of our own. Our thoughts, prayers, and deepest condolences go out to Jordan's family, friends, former teammates, and everyone whose lives she touched. In particular, her sister Jayden Scott, who graduated last May and was also a member of the Castle High School girls basketball program and Jordan's teammate at the University of Evansville. We ask our community to wrap her loved ones in support during this unimaginably difficult time. Once a Knight, always a Knight. Rest in peace, Jordan."

Scott played the 2025-26 school year at Wabash Valley College in Mount Carmel, Illinois. She started 26 of 27 games and finished third on the team with 12.5 points per game. Scott led the Warriors with 3.0 assists and 2.3 steals. Scott officially transfered to UE in June. WVC athletics posted the following on social media:

"Here at Wabash, we strive to look after our athletes as family and support them in their future endeavors after their time as a Warrior. Today, we received a phone call and learned the devastating news that former Lady Warrior and current University of Evansville Purple Ace Jordan Scott has passed away. Our prayers and condolences go to the Scott family during this time."

Her sister Jayden also signed with UE women's basketball this summer.

"We are heartbroken by Jordan's passing," UE athletic director Ziggy Siegfried said. "Jordan was a beloved member of our Purple Aces family, and we are grateful that she chose to share part of her life with us. Our hearts are especially with her sister and teammate, Jayden, their parents and family, and Jordan's teammates and coaches. We will surround them with our love, care, and support in the difficult days ahead."

Kyle Sokeland is a sports reporter for the Courier & Press. Follow him on X (formerly Twitter) @kylesokeland or email at kyle.sokeland@courierpress.com .

articles.title: Bill Belichick breaks his silence on investigation
articles.summary: The North Carolina Tar Heels football program is currently in the midst of an internal investigation that has already resulted in the departure of the team’s...
articles.body:
The North Carolina Tar Heels football program is currently in the midst of an internal investigation that has already resulted in the departure of the team's general manager and could potentially put head coach Bill Belichick's job at risk as well. Now, Belichick is addressing the investigation himself.

In a press conference on Monday, Belichick did not say much about the ongoing investigation, but he did express commitment to "doing things properly."

With Lombardi now officially out of the program, WRAL News reports that the investigation has turned its attention toward Steve Belichick, as investigators are reportedly asking questions about whether he used drugs while on the job or supplied drugs to at least one player.

"Lawyers hired to conduct the investigation are also questioning people about whether defensive coordinator Steve Belichick used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player — and, separately, about whether a member of UNC's recruiting staff had a sexual relationship with a player, people familiar with the investigation told WRAL. They also asked about possible sexual relationships between assistant coaches and recruiting staff, the people said," WRAL reported on Thursday.

Meanwhile, WRAL reports that investigators are also examining whether an unnamed member of North Carolina's recruiting staff was involved in a sexual relationship with a player.

UNC has so far declined to publicly reveal the specific purpose or scope of the Lombardi investigation.

"As is standard procedure with personnel matters, leadership, staff, and student-athletes are prohibited from addressing this topic further," the university said in a statement after the probe was announced.

Bill Belichick's Job Could Be In Jeopardy

While the investigation is reportedly focused on Steve Belichick, Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk reports that Bill Belichick's position could also be in jeopardy as a result of the ongoing investigation.

As Florio notes, the WRAL News report states that "people said they were asked whether they had reported any potentially questionable behavior to Bill Belichick." According to Florio, that line of questioning could potentially give UNC grounds to fire Bill Belichick for cause if investigators determine that he was aware of one or more of these issues and failed to report them.

Florio also shared a key section of Belichick's contract with the school, specifically Article 11(c): "Any action that is (i) taken by Coach or someone supervised by Coach, or (ii) taken at the direction of Coach or someone supervised by Coach, or (iii) known by Coach or someone supervised by Coach and not reported by Coach as required by this Agreement to the Department of Athletics Compliance office by the person supervised by coach, and that results in any material form of disciplinary finding, material action against, or material sanction for the Coach or the Program by the University's athletics association (e.g. NCAA), athletics conference (e.g. ACC), University, or other regulatory body that exceeds an institutional letter of admonishment or reprimand."

Belichick signed a five-year, $50 million contract with the school. If the investigation concludes that he failed to properly report these issues, UNC could potentially fire him for cause, which would also mean forfeiting his buyout.

Ahead of Monday's press conference, a UNC spokesperson indicated that Belichick nor anybody else would be speaking on the investigation.

"Coach Belichick, student athletes, and other university employees will not discuss the situation in any manner. That is necessary to protect the integrity of the process and the rights of everyone involved," the spokesperson said via WRAL .

Still, Belichick addressed the situation in his opening statement, saying "the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team and, obviously, our high standard here of our code of conduct and doing things the right way and making sure that our student-athletes are given the utmost, the best treatment, the very best care, and the very best coaching that we can possibly give them."

"Obviously everybody's responsible, including me, for doing things properly," Belichick said via ESPN . "And we intend to do that."
